Simulate At-Bat Outcomes Between a Pitcher and a Batter

Source: R/at_bat_sim.R
at_bat_sim.Rd

This function simulates plate appearances between a specified pitcher and batter using their Statcast data. Outcome probabilities combine the batter's, the pitcher's and the league's outcome rates with the odds-ratio (generalized log5) method, and are then adjusted for the batter's success against the sampled pitch type and location.

Usage

at_bat_sim(
  pitcher_id,
  batter_id,
  start_date,
  end_date,
  num_simulations = 1000,
  num_cores = 2,
  seed = NULL,
  league_rates = NULL,
  prior_pa = 50,
  location_prior_pa = 20,
  multiplier_range = c(0.5, 2),
  game_types = c("R", "PO"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

pitcher_id

Numeric. The ID of the pitcher (Statcast / MLBAM pitcher ID).

batter_id

Numeric. The ID of the batter (Statcast / MLBAM batter ID).

start_date

Character. The start date of the data retrieval period in "YYYY-MM-DD" format.

end_date

Character. The end date of the data retrieval period in "YYYY-MM-DD" format.

num_simulations

Numeric. The number of plate appearances to simulate. Default is 1000.

num_cores

Numeric. The number of CPU cores to use for parallel processing. Default is 2.

seed

Optional integer. When supplied, results are reproducible, including across different values of num_cores. Default NULL draws a seed from the current R session, so calling set.seed() beforehand also makes results reproducible.

league_rates

Optional named numeric vector of league outcome rates with names strikeout, walk, single, double, triple, home_run, flyout, groundout. It is normalized to sum to 1. Default NULL uses an approximate MLB average (see Details).

prior_pa

Numeric. Prior strength, in plate appearances, used to shrink each player's outcome rates toward league_rates. Default is 50.

location_prior_pa

Numeric. Prior strength, in plate appearances, used to shrink the batter's hit rate in each pitch type and location bin toward the batter's pitch-type rate, and the pitch-type rate toward the batter's overall rate. Default is 20.

multiplier_range

Numeric vector of length 2. The location/pitch-type multiplier applied to hit outcomes is clipped to this range. Default is c(0.5, 2).

game_types

Character vector of Baseball Savant game type codes to include. Default c("R", "PO") is regular season and postseason; add "S" for spring training.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, prints sample sizes and the pre-location outcome rates. Default is FALSE.

Value

A data frame with one row per outcome and columns Outcome and Probability (the share of simulated plate appearances ending in that outcome; sums to 1). The attribute "matchup" holds the inputs to the simulation: plate-appearance counts, the shrunken batter and pitcher rates, the league rates and the combined (pre-location) rates.

Details

Data. Pitch-level Statcast data for both players is downloaded from Baseball Savant for the date window. Rates are computed per plate appearance (PA): one row per PA, the row whose events is non-empty.

Outcome mapping. Statcast events are mapped to eight outcomes:

  • strikeout, strikeout_double_play become strikeout.

  • walk, intent_walk and hit_by_pitch become walk. Hit-by-pitch is folded in because it has the same result for the batter (they reach first base).

  • single, double, triple, home_run map to themselves.

  • Other in-play outs, fielder's choices, reached-on-error and sacrifices (field_out, force_out, grounded_into_double_play, double_play, triple_play, fielders_choice, fielders_choice_out, field_error, sac_fly, sac_bunt, sac_fly_double_play, sac_bunt_double_play) become groundout when bb_type == "ground_ball" and flyout otherwise (fly ball, line drive, popup).

  • Excluded: catcher_interf, and rows that do not complete a PA (truncated_pa, caught_stealing_*, pickoff_*, stolen_base_*, wild_pitch, passed_ball, other_out, other_advance, runner_double_play, game_advisory, ejection).

Combining batter and pitcher. Each player's outcome counts are shrunk toward the league rates by adding prior_pa pseudo-PAs at league rates: \(\tilde p(o) = (n_o + k\,p_{lg}(o)) / (n + k)\). The two are combined with the odds-ratio (generalized log5) rule \(p(o) \propto p_{bat}(o)\,p_{pit}(o) / p_{lg}(o)\), normalized to sum to 1.

The default league baseline is an approximate, constant MLB average per PA: strikeout 0.23, walk 0.08, single 0.15, double 0.05, triple 0.005, home run 0.03, flyout 0.20, groundout 0.24, normalized from a total of 0.985 to 1. It is not season-specific. Supply league_rates to use your own.

Pitch type and location. For each simulated PA a pitch type is sampled from the pitcher's mix of PA-ending pitches, and a location from a 2D kernel density estimate (MASS::kde2d(), 50 x 50 grid, uniform jitter within the grid cell) of the pitcher's PA-ending pitches of that type. Pitch types with fewer than 30 PA-ending pitches use the KDE of all the pitcher's PA-ending pitches. The batter's hit rate (hits per PA) is computed in 0.5 ft bins of plate_x (-2 to 2) and plate_z (0 to 5) for each pitch type, shrunk toward the batter's rate on that pitch type, which is shrunk toward the overall rate (both with location_prior_pa). The four hit outcomes are multiplied by bin rate / overall rate, clipped to multiplier_range, and the probabilities are renormalized. When the batter has no PAs in a bin, the bin rate equals the pitch-type rate; when the batter has never ended a PA on that pitch type, or the location falls outside the bins, the multiplier is 1. A missing bin never produces a strikeout. Pitch types must match exactly (for example, SI and FF are different pitches).

Main simplification. Each simulated PA is decided by one sampled decisive pitch. The count and pitch sequencing are not modeled, and there are no park, handedness or platoon adjustments beyond what is already in each player's own data. The location adjustment is relative to the batter's own average, so a pitcher's location tendencies are partly reflected both in the pitcher's outcome rates and in the multiplier.

Reproducibility. Simulations run in fixed chunks of 1000 PAs, and each chunk gets its own L'Ecuyer-CMRG random-number stream derived from seed (parallel::nextRNGStream()). Because the streams belong to the chunks rather than to the workers, the same seed gives identical results for any num_cores. The global random-number state is restored when the function returns.

A warning is issued when either player has fewer than 50 PAs in the window.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Simulate plate appearances between Gerrit Cole and Mike Trout in the 2022 season
at_bat_sim(
  pitcher_id = 543037,  # Gerrit Cole
  batter_id = 545361,   # Mike Trout
  start_date = "2022-04-01",
  end_date = "2022-10-01",
  num_simulations = 10000,
  num_cores = 2,
  seed = 42
)
#> Fetching Statcast data for pitcher 543037 ...
#> Fetching Statcast data for batter 545361 ...
#>     Outcome Probability
#> 1 strikeout      0.3593
#> 2      walk      0.0941
#> 3    single      0.0757
#> 4    double      0.0414
#> 5    triple      0.0016
#> 6  home_run      0.0903
#> 7    flyout      0.2381
#> 8 groundout      0.0995
# }
